# Cosmic UI

> A free, open-source library of sci-fi themed UI components for React and Vue.
> Components ship with angular clipped frames, glowing borders, and HUD-style
> surfaces instead of the usual rounded rectangles. Behaviour comes from Zag.js
> state machines, so components are accessible and headless underneath; the
> visual identity lives in SVG path data on a `Frame` primitive, separate from
> component logic.

Install and usage is copy-in source, not a black-box package: the component
files are written into the project and owned by it. Styling is Tailwind CSS v4.
Every component exists in both a React and a Vue version with identical markup
and visuals.

## Installing components (read this first)

Use the CLI. It resolves the dependencies between components, which is the part
that is easy to get wrong by hand:

```
npx @left4code/cosmic-ui-cli@latest init          # writes cosmic.json + design tokens
npx @left4code/cosmic-ui-cli@latest add dialog    # writes dialog AND button, frame, portal, presence
npx @left4code/cosmic-ui-cli@latest list --json   # machine-readable component list
```

Flags that matter for non-interactive use: `--yes` (never prompt),
`--no-install` (print the package-manager command instead of running it),
`--overwrite`, `--framework react|vue`, `--dir <path>`, `--alias <path>`.

Important: most components import other components. `dialog`, `menu`, `select`
and `combobox` each need `button`, `frame`, `portal` and `presence`; nearly
everything needs `frame`. Copying a single file by hand will fail to build. The
CLI handles this; if you copy manually, follow `registryDependencies`.

The components also need design tokens (`--color-primary`, the frame colours,
the type scale) in the same CSS file as `@import "tailwindcss"`. `init` writes
them; they are also at https://cosmic-ui.com/r/theme.css

## Machine-readable registry

Fetch these directly instead of scraping the docs pages:

- https://cosmic-ui.com/r/index.json - every component, its npm dependencies, its
  registry dependencies, and the URL for its full definition.
- https://cosmic-ui.com/r/{framework}/{name}.json - one component: every file with
  its complete contents, npm dependencies, and registry dependencies.
  Example: https://cosmic-ui.com/r/react/button.json
- https://cosmic-ui.com/r/theme.css - the design tokens.

Frameworks are `react` and `vue`. File paths in a registry item are relative to
the project's components directory, and imports use the `@/components` alias by
default.

## Getting started

- [How to use (React)](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/how-to-use): install steps, Tailwind setup, CSS import order.
- [How to use (Vue)](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/vue/how-to-use): same steps for Vue 3.
- [Frame](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/frame): the primitive every other component is built on. Takes an array of SVG path definitions and renders the angular border, glow, and fill.
- [Colors](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/colors): the design tokens and how to retheme.

## Components (React)

- [Accordion](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/accordion)
- [Alert](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/alert)
- [Button](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/button)
- [Chart](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/chart)
- [Checkbox](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/checkbox)
- [Combobox](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/combobox)
- [Dialog](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/dialog)
- [Input](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/input)
- [Menu](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/menu)
- [Radio Group](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/radio-group)
- [Select](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/select)
- [Switch](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/switch)
- [Tabs](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/tabs)
- [Textarea](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/textarea)
- [Toast](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/react/toast)

## Components (Vue)

Same set, same props, under `/docs/vue/` instead of `/docs/react/`. For example
[Dialog for Vue](https://cosmic-ui.com/docs/vue/dialog).

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/rizznme/cosmic-ui): MIT licensed source and issue tracker.
- [svg-renderer](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@left4code/svg-renderer): the standalone package that turns Frame path data into rendered SVG.
